pdfs.name: storage-whitepaper.pdf
pages: Abstract: we evaluate a sharded storage layout for time series data.
Related work covers LSM trees and column stores.
The benchmark ran on 8 nodes and finished in 42 minutes.
Write throughput peaked at 1.2 million points per second.
Read latency stayed flat as the dataset grew.
Compression reduced the on-disk footprint by 71 percent.
A failover test killed two nodes without data loss.
Operational cost was estimated per terabyte per month.
Memory use stayed under 2 GB per node for the whole run.
Conclusion: sharding pays off once the dataset exceeds 1 TB.

keyPoints.text: 基准测试跑在 8 个节点上，42 分钟完成
全程每个节点内存占用低于 2 GB

pages: This note collects observations from the pilot line. The line runs two shifts a day and produces roughly 300 units per shift. Scrap rate sits near 2 percent and most defects come from the coating step. Humidity in the assembly hall drifts above the tolerance band in summer. The enclosure is made of stainless steel because the previous aluminium version corroded near the coast. Tooling changes take about 40 minutes and are done between shifts. A full audit of the coating step is planned before the next production run. Operators asked for better lighting at the inspection bench. The note ends with a short list of open questions for the process team.
